Normally, throughout the day and the night, thousands of planes are taking off, crisscrossing the country, and landing. Even if no more flights took off, all of those planes needed to land. For the people below, getting them down safely became an immediate preoccupation. This type of nationwide grounding had happened only twice before in recent history—once after the September 11 attacks, and once in January 2023 for about an hour and a half. Every aircraft still aloft needed to make it to its destination, despite apparently spotty communications. Our formidable system of flight, a machine that’s constantly in motion and choreographed to the minute, has backups built in.
